s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of neurological deficits with reduced consciousness, aphasia, and urinary incontinence in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: Multiple enhancing nodular white matter lesions on brain CT scan
key_facts: 60-year-old woman
Recently diagnosed with HIV
Not yet on antiretroviral therapy
One-day history of reduced consciousness, aphasia, and urinary incontinence
Two-day history of dry cough, drenching night sweats, and weight loss
No fever, headache, neck stiffness, visual disturbances, photophobia, or seizures
Wasted appearance with weight of 40 kg
Afebrile with blood pressure 120/74 mmHg, pulse 66 beats/min, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air
Glasgow Coma Scale score of 14/15 with dysarthria
CD4 count of 6 cells/mm^3
Positive serum cryptococcal antigen test with a titer of 1:320

shortlist.label: Cryptococcal meningitis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive serum cryptococcal antigen test and multiple enhancing nodular white matter lesions on brain CT scan

shortlist.label: Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with multiple ring-enhancing lesions on brain CT scan

shortlist.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with multiple enhancing nodular white matter lesions on brain CT scan

shortlist.label: CNS tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with symptoms of weight loss, night sweats, and neurological deficits

shortlist.label: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with multiple subcortical non-enhancing hypoattenuating lesions suggestive of infarcts on brain CT scan

raw.rationale: The patient has a positive serum cryptococcal antigen test with a titer of 1:320, a very low CD4 count of 6 cells/mm^3, and symptoms consistent with CNS involvement such as reduced consciousness and aphasia, which are highly suggestive of cryptococcal meningitis.

rejected.label: Toxoplasmosis
rejected.why: While toxoplasmosis is a common opportunistic infection in HIV patients, the presence of a positive serum cryptococcal antigen test and the specific combination of symptoms and findings point more directly to cryptococcal meningitis.

rejected.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
rejected.why: This condition is less likely given the acute presentation and the specific laboratory findings, particularly the positive cryptococcal antigen test.

rejected.label: CNS tuberculosis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and the imaging findings, combined with the positive cryptococcal antigen test, make CNS tuberculosis less likely in this context.

rejected.label: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with more gradual neurological deterioration and does not explain the positive cryptococcal antigen test or the acute onset of symptoms described in the vignette.
